title: Lightfield request catalog + probe notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Short synthesis for Eng/Product: condense a mixed batch of customer feedback into a compact catalog of requests and low-effort probes.
- 'Lightfield' is our shorthand here for multi-dimensional feedback (latency x cost x quality x security) aggregated from CS calls (Sep–Oct 2025).

High-level signal summary (what customers are telling us)
- Recurring pain: unpredictable P95 latency spikes during short bursts (esp. chat workloads). Most customers see baseline latency fine, but small bursts cause timeouts or fallbacks that confuse their UX.
- Cost sensitivity shoehorns customers into aggressive batching/quantization; they worry output degradation when we suggest lower-precision variants.
- Private/Dedicated deployment friction: KMS integration steps and network egress rules are the most common blockers to onboarding.
- SDK ergonomics: customers want clearer error semantics (retry vs user-facing failure), stable typing for streaming callbacks, and a single method to pin model family + fallback policy.
- Embedding drift: a handful of analytics teams reported drift when model versions changed; they want explicit versioning and eval diffs pushed to them.

Representative customer quotes (paraphrased)
- "We see sudden latency blips that turn a microservice call into a 2s+ hit; hard to hide in our UI."
- "Your 'faster' quant model sometimes changes our reranking order; we can't accept silent quality regressions."
- "Setting up KMS in our VPC was longer than the entire pilot."

Quick numbers pulled from CS notes (approx)
- ~12 enterprise customers reported burst P95 > 1s above baseline in the last 6 weeks.
- ~8 customers delayed private deployment due to KMS/network docs gaps.
- ~6 teams asked explicitly for per-model pre-release eval diffs.

Root-cause hypotheses (why these keep recurring)
- Serving runtime: single-tenant scheduling + autoscaler thresholds sometimes cause queueing when short concurrent bursts occur.
- Kernel selection: in some cases runtime picks a kernel path optimized for throughput which penalizes short sequences and chat-style patterns.
- Observability: customers lack visibility into which fallback path (model variant/region) served a request — they see only the user-facing outcome.
- Docs & SRE handoff: KMS/network steps are semantically correct but scattered across multiple pages; customers need a single executable checklist.

Candidate quick probes (low-effort experiments to validate & mitigate)
1) Probe: Burst SLO telemetry badge (2-week pilot)
   - What: expose a per-customer 'burst P95' metric in Console for top 10 customers.
   - Why: validate frequency & impact; give CS a talking point.
   - Owner: observability team + CS; effort: small (2–3 engineer days).

2) Probe: 'Fail open' vs 'Fail closed' toggle test (canary)
   - What: let customers opt into a config that prefers lower-cost fallback variants *without* silent quality masking; surface a quality delta in responses.
   - Why: assess whether visible tradeoffs reduce silent regressions and align expectations.
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + serving-runtime; effort: moderate (1 sprint).

3) Probe: KMS quickstart checklist + runbook doc + 1-hour onboarding offer
   - What: one consolidated page + short script for common KMS providers; CS offers a 1-hour assisted onboarding call.
   - Why: remove onboarding friction for Private deployments.
   - Owner: private-deployments + customer-success; effort: low.

4) Probe: SDK error taxonomy and streaming callback contract (alpha)
   - What: release an SDK patch that standardizes error types (Transient vs Permanent) and provides a single stream API with typed events.
   - Why: reduce customer mis-retries and simplify UX for streaming.
   - Owner: developer-experience; effort: 2 sprints.

5) Probe: Pre-release model-diff email seed
   - What: for customers subscribed to a model, send a short diff summary (latency/cost/accuracy on key evals) when we plan to change model weight/quantization.
   - Why: prevents surprise regressions and reduces rollback churn.
   - Owner: product + applied-ml; effort: minimal (parse existing eval artifacts).

Priority-impact matrix (subjective initial ranking)
- High impact / low effort: KMS checklist + onboarding call; Burst SLO telemetry badge; Pre-release model-diff email.
- High impact / medium effort: SDK error taxonomy; Fail-open toggle with surfaced quality deltas.
- Medium impact / low effort: Small docs consolidations on kernel choices and sequence-length best practices.

Concrete next steps for the week (Oct 6–10)
- CS to run short interviews (15–20 min) with 6 affected customers to gather example timelines of burst events and attach request IDs where possible (owner: Maya).
- Observability to prototype a burst-P95 view for internal testing (owner: Priya).
- Private deployments + Docs to produce a single KMS quickstart page and a checklist; schedule a pilot assisted onboarding for 2 customers (owner: Luis).
- Developer-experience to draft an SDK error taxonomy doc and circulate (owner: Samir).

Open questions / unknowns
- How many customers would accept visible quality tradeoffs if we provide clear diffs? (need to quantify willingness-to-compromise)
- Does the autoscaler change recently rolled out (Aug) contribute to bursts? (eng team take a look at config history)
- What is the true customer scope for pre-release diffs? All model changes or only quant/architecture shifts?

Potential risks and mitigations
- Risk: surfacing quality diffs may cause alarm and churn. Mitigation: start with an opt-in set of customers and short explanatory messaging.
- Risk: SDK surface changes cause backward compatibility issues. Mitigation: alpha channel + migration guide.

Appendix: example customer timeline (from a support ticket)
- 2025-09-12 14:23 UTC: Customer X reports UI slowdown, correlates with multiple user messages sent almost simultaneously.
- 2025-09-12 14:23–14:25 UTC: Our traces show a 1.6s spike in P95; fallback to a smaller-capacity region occurred.
- 2025-09-12 14:30 UTC: CS suggested increasing reserved concurrency; customer says that raises cost beyond acceptable levels.

Notes to self
- Add links to the telemetry dataset and the exact JIRA tickets after the customer interviews.
- Keep this doc living; convert to a short Confluence if probes move to implementation.

---
Document end.
